extracted.intended_audience: FOIA/Privacy Act requesters and agency FOIA/Privacy Act staff (requesters seeking Commission records; Commission personnel handling requests/appeals)
extracted.subtask_short: FOIA and Privacy Act requests to Commission
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and standards for requesting, accessing, amending, and appealing disclosure of records under the Privacy Act of 1974 and the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) from the National Commission on Military, National, and Public Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules implement the Privacy Act (5 U.S.C. 552a(f)) for Commission systems of records retrieved by an individual’s name or other identifying particular and establish procedures to determine whether a system contains records about an individual, to gain access, and to request correction or amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules apply to all records maintained by the Commission that are retrieved by name or identifying number; should be read together with the Privacy Act text for additional information about records maintained on individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of key terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines terms used in the part (e.g., business day; Chair; Commission; Commission system; General Counsel; Individual; Privacy Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business day means calendar day excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays; Individual means a U.S. citizen or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence; other titles may mean the official or designee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of contact for Privacy Act inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquiries about systems of records or implementation of the Privacy Act should be sent to the Office of the General Counsel at the specified Commission address and phone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mailing address and telephone hours (business days, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for requesting access to Privacy Act records (§426.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may request notification if a named system of records contains records pertaining to you and may review such records by writing to the Office of the General Counsel or scheduling an in-person appointment by phone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be in writing and identify the Commission system(s); requests treated as both Privacy Act and FOIA requests; telephone scheduling available; call number provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of access and copy limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to records or other information will be provided if identification requirements (§426.105) are satisfied and the records are releasable; the Commission will provide an opportunity to have a copy made and will supply only one copy of each requested record based on fee schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If record must be copied to provide access (e.g., computer printout), the copy will be provided without cost; only one copy supplied; fee schedule in §426.108 applies for copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness for processing access requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission will comply promptly with in-person requests if requirements are met and records are available; will acknowledge mailed or non-immediately-available requests within 10 business days and provide information promptly thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgement timeline: 10 business days for mailed or personal requests not immediately available; prompt provision once available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompaniment and representatives during review
rubrics_metrics.description: If you make your request in person you may be accompanied by a person of your choice to review your records; Commission may require a written statement authorizing discussion in the accompanying person’s presence; records may be disclosed to a representative upon proper written consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission may require written authorization; representative disclosure requires proper written consent from you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical and psychological records disclosure rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical or psychological records pertaining to you shall be disclosed to you unless Commission judges access might have an adverse effect upon you; in such cases Commission may refuse direct disclosure and instead disclose through a licensed physician designated by you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where adverse-effect determination is made, disclosure may be via a licensed physician you designate in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal adverse Privacy Act determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: If unsatisfied with an adverse determination on your request to access records, you may appeal using the procedures in §426.107(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §426.107 for appeal timing and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements when requesting access (§426.105)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission requires reasonable identification of all individuals requesting access to ensure records are disclosed to the proper person; amount varies with record sensitivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-person disclosure generally requires photo ID (e.g., driver’s license with photograph and signature); for particularly sensitive records Commission may require additional means (e.g., oath, signed statement) and warn of criminal penalties (5 U.S.C. 552a(i)(3); 18 U.S.C. 1001). Mail requests may require signed, notarized statements or statements under oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for amending or correcting records (§426.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are entitled to request amendments or corrections of records you believe are not accurate, relevant, timely, or complete; requests should be in writing to the Office of the General Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request should specify the particular record, the Commission system, the precise correction or amendment (preferably an edited copy reflecting desired modification), and reasons for the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement and processing timeline for amendment requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission will acknowledge a request for amendment or correction within 10 business days unless it can be processed and the individual informed within that 10-day period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If General Counsel agrees record is not accurate/timely/complete based on preponderance of evidence, record will be corrected/amended promptly or deleted if not relevant/necessary, and you will be informed in writing; prior recipients will be informed of corrective action where accounting was made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of amendment requests and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: If General Counsel does not agree to amend/correct, you will be informed in writing of the refusal and the reason and that you may appeal under §426.107.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests governed by another agency’s regulations will be forwarded to that agency and you will be informed of the referral in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Chair for refusal to amend (§426.107)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may appeal a refusal to amend or correct a record to the Chair in writing within 30 business days of receipt of the initial refusal; appeal should indicate basis for appeal and be sent to the Office of the General Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair reviews request, General Counsel’s refusal, and other pertinent material; no hearing will be held; Chair shall render decision within 30 business days unless extended for good cause with written notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes of amendment appeals and statements of disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: If Chair determines record should be amended/corrected, the record will be modified and prior recipients notified where appropriate; if appeal denied you may submit a concise statement of disagreement which will be disclosed with the record in subsequent disclosures and the record annotated as disputed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial notice will inform you of ability to seek judicial review under 5 U.S.C. 552a(g)(1); Commission may also disclose a concise statement of Chair’s reasons for denial alongside the disputed record (that statement will not be subject to correction).

rubrics_metrics.name: No fees for search/review time; copying fees policy (§426.108)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission will charge no fees for search time or other time expended to review a record; may charge where you request copies of records to which you have been granted access; copies necessary to provide access (e.g., printouts) are provided without cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photocopy rate: $0.12 per page; non-photocopiable materials charged at actual cost; copying fees not charged if cost of collecting fee would be equal/greater than fee; contemporaneous copies aggregated to determine total fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special and additional services fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Special/additional services at request (e.g., certification/authentication, postal insurance, special mailing) charged at market rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charged to requester when provided at their request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waiver or reduction for indigent requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: You may request a copying fee not be charged or be reduced by submitting a written petition to the General Counsel asserting indigence; General Counsel may waive or reduce fees at his/her discretion if resources permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General Counsel evaluates petition and may waive or reduce copying fee based on indigence and Commission resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment before copying
rubrics_metrics.description: All fees shall be paid before any copying request is undertaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees must be paid in advance of copying work being performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting of disclosures (§426.109)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of the General Counsel shall maintain a log containing date, nature, and purpose of each disclosure of a record to any person or another agency, including the name and address of recipient; excludes disclosures to Commission employees in official duties or pursuant to FOIA provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention: accounting retained at least five years after disclosure or for life of the record; accounting made available to the individual on request except for disclosures made for law enforcement purposes under 5 U.S.C. 552a(b)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: General FOIA implementation and reading of FOIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart B contains Commission regulations implementing the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), 5 U.S.C. 552; regulations should be read together with the FOIA text and OMB Uniform FOIA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets forth procedures for requesting access to Commission records under FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive disclosures and website availability (§426.202)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records FOIA requires agencies to make available for public inspection in electronic format may be accessed through the Commission’s website; the Commission will ensure the website of posted records and indices is reviewed and updated on an ongoing basis; a FOIA Public Liaison is available to assist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Website provided (www.inspire2serve.gov) and FOIA Public Liaison contact availability noted; encourages checking website before making formal FOIA request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of records routinely available without formal FOIA request
rubrics_metrics.description: The following records shall be available routinely on the website unless exempt: (1) formal reports issued by the Commission; (2) testimonies and presentations submitted; (3) schedules for public meetings/hearings with transcripts or notes; (4) press statements; (5) substantive rules, procedural rules of general operations, statements of general policy or interpretations; (6) copies of previously released records likely to be subject of subsequent requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When three or more requests for substantially the same records are received, the Commission shall make the released records available in the reading room and on the website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reading room requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission shall maintain a public reading room at Commission offices containing records available for public inspection that cannot be produced electronically; reading room available workdays 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; appointments via FOIA Public Liaison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading room provides access to non-electronic records; appointments arranged through FOIA Public Liaison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction and explanation requirement (§426.202(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission may redact information based on FOIA exemptions before making information available or publishing; the justification for redaction must be explained in writing and the extent of redaction indicated on the record unless doing so would harm an interest protected by the exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The location of deleted information must be indicated on the record if technically feasible; explanation of redaction must be provided in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirements for making FOIA requests (§426.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission encourages checking website for documents before making a request; for records not on website the Commission shall promptly provide records to any person in response to a request that conforms to the rules and procedures of this section; FOIA Public Liaison available to assist in describing records sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt provision applies except where records are already available or subject to FOIA exemptions/exclusions; FOIA Public Liaison can help reformulate requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and submission of FOIA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for records not available on the website should be submitted in writing by mail or via internet (website or email); mail address and recommended email (FOIA@inspire2serve.gov) provided; Commission will communicate by email unless requester specifies otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters may specify preferred form or format and Commission will accommodate if record is readily reproducible in that form/format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of a FOIA request (§426.203(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must include requester’s full name, mailing address, telephone number, and email (if any); a description of records sought in enough detail to allow location (date, title, author, recipient, subject matter, file designations if known); if claiming special requester category (educational, non-commercial scientific, news media) include supporting information; fee waiver request if applicable; statement explaining need for expedited processing if requested; verification of identity for records about oneself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The more specific the description, the easier it is to locate records; verification required for Privacy Act requests as per subpart A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfected request / date received (§426.203(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission deems it has received a request on the date it receives a request containing the required information; if request does not reasonably describe records, agency must inform requester what additional information is needed and assist via FOIA Public Liaison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters attempting to reformulate or modify a request may discuss with FOIA Public Liaison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of responsive records (§426.204(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining which records are responsive, an agency ordinarily includes only records in its possession as of the date it begins its search; records excluded from FOIA under 5 U.S.C. 552(c) are not considered responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any date other than search start date is used, agency must inform requester of that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to grant or deny FOIA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief FOIA Officer or designee is authorized to grant or deny requests for records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chief FOIA Officer handles determinations and denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation, referral, and coordination with other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing records, Commission will determine whether another federal agency is better able to determine whether the record is exempt; options include consultation (originating agency consults another agency), referral (refer responsibility to another agency), or coordination (where revealing the identity of the agency could harm protected interests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referrals must be documented, a copy of the record retained, and requester notified of the referral and contact; coordination is used when revealing the referral agency could harm exemptions (privacy, national security), and the originating agency conveys release determination to requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of consultations/referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: All consultations and referrals received by the Commission will be handled according to the date the first agency received the perfected FOIA request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date for timing purposes is the date the first agency received the perfected request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of FOIA responses and acknowledgements (§426.205 & §426.206)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission will ordinarily respond by order of receipt: (1) provide acknowledgment with tracking number and summary within 10 working days of a perfected request; (2) ordinarily have 20 work days to determine whether to grant or deny a request; (3) appeal decisions within 20 work days after receipt of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 20-day period may be tolled for one reasonable demand for clarifying information or while awaiting requester’s response to fee assessment; acknowledgements include tracking number, date of receipt, fee waiver/ reduction info, and summary of records requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-track processing system
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests assigned to Standard, Complex, or Expedited tracks based on complexity; Standard for routine requests with little search/review time; Complex for non-routine, voluminous, or high-effort requests; Expedited for requests meeting expedited criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard Track: respond in order received, aim within 20 working days; Complex Track: notify requester if assigned and give estimate; may discuss reformulation; Expedited Track: follow expedited processing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited processing requirements and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Expedited processing must accompany the initial request, be clearly marked and contain a certified written statement of compelling need; Commission decides within 10 calendar days whether to grant expedited status and gives priority if granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for expedited processing include: (1) imminent threat to life/physical safety if records not obtained; (2) urgency to inform the public about actual/alleged federal government activity for persons primarily engaged in disseminating information; (3) reasonable expectation of imminent loss of a substantial due process right. Denials of expedited processing can be appealed like other denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unusual circumstances extension
rubrics_metrics.description: If 'unusual circumstances' exist as defined in FOIA, response/appeal time limits may be extended by no more than 10 work days with written notice to the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must include reason for extension, expected determination date, availability of FOIA Public Liaison, and right to seek dispute resolution from OGIS; requester may be offered options to limit scope or arrange alternate timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response practices and interim/rolling disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request involves voluminous material or searches in multiple locations, the agency may provide interim responses and release records on a rolling basis; Commission will provide an estimated date for response upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgement will include an estimated date for response; rolling releases used to reduce delay for voluminous requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant notices for FOIA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a FOIA Officer grants a request in full or part, Commission shall promptly provide written notice of the decision, applicable fees under section 10, and availability of FOIA Public Liaison; also notify requester of track assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice should indicate what fees apply and liaison help available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a denial notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Denial notices must include: (1) name and title/position of person responsible for denial; (2) brief statement of reasons including any FOIA exemption applied; (3) description of material withheld (approximate number of pages or reasonable estimation); (4) statement that denial may be appealed under section 8(a) and description of appeal requirements; (5) notice of assistance available from FOIA Public Liaison and OGIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial may include decisions that fees are not waived, no expedited processing, no responsive records, record destroyed, or records exempt in whole or part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction notation practice for withheld portions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a portion of a record is withheld, the amount of information redacted and the claimed exemption will be noted at the place in the record where the redaction was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps requester understand where and why information was withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of confidential commercial information and submitter
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential commercial information means commercial or financial information obtained from a submitter that may be protected under FOIA Exemption 4; submitter includes any person or entity (corporation, State, foreign government, but not another Federal Government entity) that provides such information to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term identifies records potentially protected under Exemption 4 and who may claim protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation requirement for confidential commercial information
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitter must use good faith efforts to mark portions of submissions they consider protected under Exemption 4 at the time of submission; such designations expire 10 years after submission unless submitter requests and justifies a longer period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should mark and justify protection and can request longer designation periods with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitter notice when confidential commercial information requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission must promptly provide written notice to the submitter whenever records containing designated confidential commercial information are requested under FOIA and the agency determines it may be required to disclose such records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must describe the commercial information requested or include a copy of requested records/portions; for voluminous submitters, Commission may post or publish notice in a manner reasonably likely to inform submitters instead of sending individual notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to submitter notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: There are specified exceptions where the notice requirements do not apply (text truncated in chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page indicates exceptions exist; details follow in subsequent text (not included in this chunk).
